# Example: what a finished Boots system looks like

A generic, self-contained example the router shows on a user's first run, so the
finish line is legible before they've built anything. Render it in plain words —
never show the raw stage vocabulary. Keep it short; it's a picture, not a tour.

The story to tell (adapt the wording to the user, keep the shape):

> **Where it started —** someone said: *"I waste twenty minutes after every meeting
> turning my messy notes into a list of what we decided and who's doing what."* Fuzzy
> wish, no tool.
>
> **What Boots did —** walked it from that sentence to a small, finished thing:
> figured out the real outcome (decisions + owners, not a summary), cut it to the
> smallest useful version, built it, then **closed it** — checked it for gaps, ran it
> on a real messy note to prove it actually worked, and shipped it.
>
> **What they have now —** a skill they just say `tidy-notes` to. Paste the mess in,
> get back a clean list of decisions and who owns each. It lives on their machine and
> it's theirs. Done means *a thing you have*, not a thread you're still carrying.

The one line that makes the point: **"That's the finish line — not a summary of an
idea, a working tool you keep. That's where I'm taking whatever you want to build."**
